public_rationale: OpenAI introduced GPT-5 on August 7, 2025, so it did not come in 2024. On reception, The Week, summarizing Bloomberg, reported that the much-anticipated rollout was 'so poorly received' that OpenAI had to restore an older model for displeased users. That matches the plain reading of 'disappointing' as falling short of expectations. OpenAI described GPT-5 as state of the art on many benchmarks, so the disappointment was about expectations and the launch, not a lack of any improvement.
limitations: 'Disappointing' is evaluative; reactions were mixed, not unanimous.
The Week is a secondary roundup; the Axios report could not be read.

our_interpretation: 'Didn't come in 2024' is checked against GPT-5's public release date.
Plain reading of 'disappointing': GPT-5's launch was widely received as falling short of expectations and the hype around it. It does not mean the model failed to improve on earlier ones.
criteria.support_condition: GPT-5 was released after 2024, and reputable coverage reports a widely disappointed or poor reception relative to expectations.
criteria.contradiction_condition: GPT-5 was released in 2024, or the launch was broadly received as meeting or beating expectations.
